correctness.rationale: The polar decomposition and iterate formula are proved by induction. For a positive d-step weighted shift, both sides of the p-hyponormal inequality are diagonal, giving an iff monotonicity criterion. The tail implication is a two-step inequality, and the threshold examples satisfy the criterion exactly. No finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The focal full text was inspected at the weighted-shift example and searched for iteration; it gives only the one-step formula. The original 2005 transform paper was inspected and contains one-step and weighted-shift results but no dyadic iterate-threshold classification. Ten semantic database queries covering the exact formula, aliases, threshold realizability, and the focal source returned no statement that implies the claim. The closest hits concern weighted-shift norm profiles or multishift self-commutators and are logically orthogonal.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete dynamical classification for iterating the source-defined transform on its canonical weighted-shift test class: the entire dependence on arbitrary positive transform exponents and on p disappears, successful iterates form a sharp tail, and every possible threshold including never is realized. This goes beyond a routine one-parameter substitution by identifying the exact iteration law and all possible hyponormalization times.
